question: After the start line, where brew's step is carried (layers 36-50), do the lenses read the intermediate I, against a distractor colour equally present in the prompt?
why: Chosen by the human (Zach, 2026-10-15) after exp07: does the lens read the intermediate where it cannot write the step? Part A's readout protocol (top-1 among candidates, distractor control, logit-lens baseline).
positions: after_start (the 21 tokens after the start line, as exp04 and exp07)

readers.logit: the final norm and unembedding applied to the block output (part A's baseline)
readers.code: exp07's code (window layers only): colour k scores <h - w_0, E_I[k]> - |E_I[k]|^2 / 2 at each position, without the item's S and A

readout: each reader's scores for the 12 palette colours' concept tokens at each position; a role is read at a position if its colour is the top-1 of the 12 (part A's 'top-1 among the candidates')

roles.X: the distractor: exp03's swap target, a rule-table colour off the path

decision.read_score: per item, the share of (window layer, position) cells at which the role's colour is top-1; differences are paired bootstraps over items (95%)
decision.reads: a reader reads the intermediate at the window if I's read score exceeds X's (CI above 0), on the fresh items (J++ primary; the J-lens, the logit lens and the code secondary; the bank items replicate)
decision.reader_works: positive control: a lens reader is interpreted only if, at the last position at layer 62, A is top-1 for more items than X (Wilson intervals not overlapping)

deviations: X is exp03's swap target, so the distractor is the colour the lens edits moved toward; any rule-table colour is equally present in the prompt.
Top-1 among 12 colours, not among the vocabulary; the vocabulary rank of I is kept for reference.
